events.title: PHP 8.4 released
events.summary: PHP 8.4 shipped on November 21, 2024 with property hooks, asymmetric visibility, and `#[\Deprecated]` attributes.
events.about: Property hooks let Laravel and Symfony models define get/set logic inline without boilerplate accessors. Asymmetric visibility (public read, private write) cleaned up DTOs and value objects — keeping PHP competitive for web APIs and CMS plugins as hosts pushed 8.x adoption.

narrative.whyChosen: PHP 8.4 added OOP ergonomics that Java and C# users take for granted.
narrative.whyImportant: Property hooks reduce magic-method hacks in frameworks and ORMs.
narrative.problemSolved: PHP classes needed verbose getter/setter pairs or `__get` magic for computed properties.

events.title: .NET 9 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET 9 on November 12, 2024 with performance tuning, AI building blocks, and C# 13 language features.
events.about: .NET 9 continued the annual release cadence after .NET 8 LTS: faster [JIT] and GC, improved ASP.NET Core, and Tensor primitives for ML workloads. Teams use it for greenfield apps while .NET 8 remains the supported LTS choice through 2026.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET 9 kept the platform current between LTS releases with AI and cloud focus.
narrative.whyImportant: Built-in tensor types signaled .NET's push into on-device and server AI inference.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers on .NET 8 LTS needed a path to newer APIs without waiting two years.

events.title: C# 13 released with .NET 9
events.summary: C# 13 shipped with .NET 9 on November 12, 2024 — adding `params` collections, a new `lock` type, and partial properties.
events.about: C# 13's `params` spans and collections simplified APIs that accept variable arguments; the new `lock` type and partial properties improved concurrency and code generation ergonomics. Paired with .NET 9's performance work, it kept C# current for cloud and AI workloads.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 13 refined collection parameters, partial properties, and lock ergonomics for modern .NET APIs.
narrative.whyImportant: Params collections reduced boilerplate in logging, formatting, and DSL APIs.
narrative.problemSolved: Variable-argument APIs required array allocations or `params object[]` workarounds.

events.title: Model Context Protocol announced
events.summary: Anthropic announced the Model Context Protocol on November 25, 2024 — an [open standard] for connecting AI assistants to tools, databases, and external data.
events.about: MCP defined a [client-server] wire format so one integration works across Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Copilot — replacing ad-hoc function-calling plugins. Within a year it became the de facto standard for agent tooling before Anthropic donated it to the Linux Foundation.

narrative.whyChosen: MCP unified how LLMs call external tools instead of every vendor inventing its own [API].
narrative.whyImportant: A shared protocol let IDEs and SaaS products ship AI integrations once.
narrative.problemSolved: Each AI product built incompatible tool-calling layers for the same databases and APIs.
